rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap and handling requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a capped screening fee (max $68.96 for 2026) and must give a receipt, itemization, credit report copy, and refund of unused portions. No fee may be charged if no unit is available, and fees must be returned to unselected applicants unless a first-come, first-qualified policy is used.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords charging prospective residential tenants a screening or application fee in California.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they: (1) review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and (2) do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.
rules.conflict_note: Fee cap amount is adjusted annually for CPI; $68.96 is the 2026 figure stated by the Berkeley Rent Board. Reusable screening report requirement mentioned on the page derives from related state law (Civ. Code § 1950.1), not cited here.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees
rules.requirement: Owners charging a fee for a credit report or to process an application must provide, in the application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of residential rental property in Berkeley who charge applicants a screening/application fee.
rules.quoted_span: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or requests to add or replace a roommate. Applies regardless of contrary lease language.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of residential rental property in Berkeley with respect to existing tenants; applies to all rental agreements regardless of contrary contract terms (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
